questions.question: That's strange, our kids ________ watch TV serials. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: Plural subject 'our kids' takes 'do not' before the base verb 'watch' to express a habitual negative statement.

questions.question: They ________ here next week. (Choose the correct verb form)
questions.explanation: 'Next week' indicates future time, so simple future 'will come' is correct.

questions.question: Marsha is reading a novel. (Choose the best passive voice)
options: A novel was read by Marsha.
A novel had read by Marsha.
A novel is being read by Marsha.
A novel must read by Marsha.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active ('is reading') changes to 'is being read' in passive voice.

questions.question: Drivers ________ drive over the speed limit. (Choose the correct option of auxiliary verb)
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses a strict rule or prohibition against exceeding the speed limit.

questions.question: "What do you want?" she asked him. (Choose the correct indirect narration)
options: She asked him what he wanted.
She will ask what he wants.
She asked what he had wanted.
questions.explanation: Past reporting verb 'asked' shifts simple present 'do you want' to simple past 'he wanted' in indirect speech.

questions.question: You must start now. You will miss the bus. (Choose the correct combination of sentences)
options: Unless you start now, you will miss the bus.
Will you start now, you will miss the bus.
Till you start now, you will miss the bus.
Until you start now, you will miss the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Unless you start now, you will miss the bus.' expresses the negative condition accurately.

questions.question: The doctor suggested ________ take a vacation. (Choose the meaningful expression)
questions.explanation: 'Suggested that the patient should take a vacation' is the grammatically complete clause structure.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have a homework to do.
I will have homework to do.
questions.explanation: 'Homework' is uncountable and does not take 'a'; 'I have homework to do.' is correct.

questions.question: When Sita ________ back, we will discuss the problem. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: Future time clause beginning with 'when' uses simple present ('comes') while the main clause uses 'will discuss'.

questions.question: ________ he come with us? (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Will he come with us?' is a proper future interrogative question.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish were I young again.
I wish was I young again.
I wish I were young again.
I wish I was young again.
questions.explanation: Unreal/hypothetical wishes after 'I wish' take 'were' in standard formal grammar ('I wish I were young again.').

questions.question: Have you seen ________ Taj Mahal. (Choose the best option of article)
questions.explanation: Definite article 'the' is used before unique historical monuments like the Taj Mahal.

questions.question: The great scholar and poet ________ died. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: A single article 'The' before two nouns joined by 'and' refers to one person, taking singular 'has died'.

questions.question: John ________ in hospital for two weeks. (Choose the meaningful expression)
questions.explanation: 'For two weeks' indicates duration up to the present, requiring 'has been lying'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She is the girl whose name is Raavi.
She is the girl whom name is Raavi.
She is the girl who name is Raavi.
She is the girl that name is Raavi.
questions.explanation: Possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is used before 'name'.

questions.question: The house was painted by Tom. (Choose the best Active voice)
questions.explanation: 'Was painted' is simple past passive, so active voice is simple past 'Tom painted the house.'

questions.question: I ________ speak Spanish. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: Subject 'I' takes 'do not' with the base verb 'speak'.

questions.question: Either of the two ________ acceptable. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Either of the two' is grammatically singular and takes 'is'.

questions.question: A lot of energy ________ wasted on finding the treasure. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Energy' is an uncountable noun, so it takes singular 'was'.

questions.question: Those who work in the same department are ________.
questions.explanation: People who work together in the same organization or department are called 'colleagues'.

questions.question: I am ________ my bed. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Am + V-ing' ('making') forms the present continuous tense.

questions.question: Listen! Radha ________ the sitar. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' signals an action happening right now, requiring singular present continuous 'is playing'.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Committee' has double 'm', double 't', and double 'e'.

questions.question: The man was ________ by a dog. (Choose the meaningful expression)
questions.explanation: Passive voice 'was + V3' requires the past participle 'bitten'.

questions.question: Look ________ this painting. (Choose the correct preposition)
questions.explanation: 'Look at' is used when directing one's gaze at something specific.

questions.question: He ________ video games. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: Singular subject 'He' takes 'is playing'.

questions.question: I bought these books ________ auction. (Choose the correct preposition)
questions.explanation: The standard phrase is 'at auction'.

questions.question: When the sun is shining, we usually ________ for swimming. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Usually' indicates a habitual action, so simple present 'go' is used with 'we'.

questions.question: Radha asked Ravi where his father was. (Choose the correct direct narration)
options: Radha said to Ravi, "Where is your father."
Radha said to Ravi, "Where is your father?"
Radha said to Ravi, "Where was his father?"
questions.explanation: Indirect question 'where his father was' converts back to direct question 'Where is your father?'

questions.question: Patna is situated ________ the bank of the Ganga. (Choose the correct preposition)
questions.explanation: The standard phrase for a location along a river's edge is 'on the bank of'.

questions.question: John Donne is a ________ poet. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: John Donne is foremost among the metaphysical poets.

questions.question: The line 'In hearts at peace, under an English heaven' is taken from ________.
questions.explanation: This line appears in Rupert Brooke's poem 'The Soldier'.

questions.question: 'Macbeth' and 'Julius Caesar' are written by ________.
questions.explanation: Both 'Macbeth' and 'Julius Caesar' are plays by William Shakespeare.

questions.question: English used since AD 1500 is called ________.
questions.explanation: The Modern English period conventionally begins around AD 1500.

questions.question: Our forefathers did not invent machinery because ________.
options: they knew we would become slaves.
they knew we would be happy.
they did not like to see us comfortable.
questions.explanation: In 'Indian Civilization and Culture', Mahatma Gandhi notes our forefathers avoided machinery knowing it would make us slaves and lose moral fibre.

questions.question: The Great Vowel Shift took place during ________.
questions.explanation: The Great Vowel Shift occurred during the transition from Middle English to Early Modern English (around 1400–1700).

questions.question: The line 'And the nightingale is dumb' is taken from ________.
options: Now the Leaves are Falling Fast
Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe
questions.explanation: This line is from W.H. Auden's poem 'Now the Leaves are Falling Fast'.

questions.question: And as we walk, we make the pledge that we shall ________.
questions.explanation: In 'I Have a Dream', Martin Luther King Jr. says we make the pledge that we shall always march ahead.

questions.question: Seibei's hobby was collecting ________.
questions.explanation: In 'The Artist', Seibei loved collecting and polishing gourds.

questions.question: The line 'Hoping to cease not till death' is taken from ________.
questions.explanation: This line is from Walt Whitman's 'Song of Myself'.

questions.question: The sentence 'After all, there is something in Hinduism that has kept it alive up till now' is taken from ________.
questions.explanation: This sentence appears in Mahatma Gandhi's 'Indian Civilization and Culture'.

questions.question: 'Savitri' is written by ________.
questions.explanation: 'Savitri: A Legend and a Symbol' is an epic poem by Sri Aurobindo (Aurobindo Ghosh).

questions.question: Bertrand Russell was awarded Nobel Prize in literature in the year ________.
questions.explanation: Bertrand Russell received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950.

questions.question: 'The Waste Land' has been composed by ________.
questions.explanation: 'The Waste Land' (1922) was written by T.S. Eliot.

questions.question: Dr. Radhakrishnan never lost his faith in the ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Bharat is My Home', Dr. Zakir Hussain notes Dr. Radhakrishnan never lost his faith in the essential humanity of man.

questions.question: New varieties of English that have emerged in different parts of the world is called ________.
questions.explanation: Emerging regional varieties of English around the world are termed 'New Englishes'.

questions.question: English language is ________ than Sanskrit and Persian.
questions.explanation: Sanskrit and Persian are ancient classical languages, making English younger in historical origin.

questions.question: Walter de la Mare makes us aware of the ________.
questions.explanation: Walter de la Mare is known for his sensitivity to human/inhuman conditions and fleeting beauty.

questions.question: Walter de la Mare was born in the year ________.
questions.explanation: Walter de la Mare was born in 1873.

questions.question: 'Ideas that Have Helped Mankind' is written by ________.
questions.explanation: 'Ideas that Have Helped Mankind' is written by Bertrand Russell.

questions.question: Write an essay in about 150 words on any one of the following: (a) Hostel life (b) The season you like most (c) Your aim in life (d) Newspaper (e) The future of English in India
questions.explanation: Subjective essay writing question (~150 words).

questions.question:
Explain any one of the following:
(a) "You're an idiot!" he shouted. "There is absolutely no future for a boy like you."
(b) "What! That means he will be here for weeks! Ministers don't see people for weeks......months! Oh, my God!"
(c) "You two'd better hurry up and get married...........Just do me a favour and leave me in peace."
questions.explanation: (a) From 'The Artist' by Shiga Naoya. (b) From 'A Pinch of Snuff' by Manohar Malgonkar. (c) From 'A Marriage Proposal' by Anton Chekhov.

questions.question:
Explain any one of the following:
(a) "When thou sigh'st thou sigh'st not winde, But sigh'st my soule away".
(b) I celebrate myself, and sing myself, and what I assume you shall assume, for every atom belonging to me as good belongs to you.
(c) Macavity, Macavity, there's no one like Macavity.
questions.explanation: (a) From 'Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe' by John Donne. (b) From 'Song of Myself' by Walt Whitman. (c) From 'Macavity: The Mystery Cat' by T.S. Eliot.

questions.question:
Attempt any one of the following:
(a) Write a letter to your cousin, asking him about the preparation of his/her upcoming examination.
(b) Write an application to the Principal of your school/college, requesting him for permission to organize a cultural event in your school/college.
questions.explanation: Subjective letter/application writing question.

questions.question:
Answer in about 40 to 50 words, any five of the following:
(a) Why did our ancestors dissuade us from luxuries and pleasures?
(b) How did Seibei's father react to the teacher's complaint?
(c) Why does Dr. Zakir Hussain call India "The young state of an ancient people"?
(d) What was the great lesson that India had to teach the west?
(e) In the poem 'An Epitaph', what will happen when the poet dies?
(f) Why is Macavity termed a 'criminal'?
(g) Why was the speaker in 'My Grandmother's House' proud of living in that house?
(h) What did the Fire Hymn say to the speaker?
(i) What are the features of a novel?
(j) Why are the Indians quick learners of English?
questions.explanation: Short answer questions (40-50 words each, any 5).

questions.question: Write a summary of any one of the following poems in about 100 words: (i) To Autumn (ii) The Soldier (iii) My Grandmother's House
questions.explanation: Subjective poetry summary question (~100 words).

questions.question: Write a summary of any one of the following prose-pieces in about 100 words: (i) A Pinch of Snuff (ii) Bharat is My Home (iii) Ideas That Have Helped Mankind
questions.explanation: Subjective prose summary question (~100 words).

questions.question: Write a note on the future of English in India. OR Write a note on the development of Indian poetry in English. OR How can we improve our English?
questions.explanation: Subjective note/composition question on Story of English.

questions.question: Match the poet 'Rupert Brooke' with the appropriate work:
options: Now the Leaves Are Falling Fast
Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe
questions.explanation: Rupert Brooke wrote 'The Soldier'.

questions.question: Match the poet 'Walt Whitman' with the appropriate work:
options: Now the Leaves Are Falling Fast
Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe
questions.explanation: Walt Whitman wrote 'Song of Myself'.

questions.question: Match the poet 'W.H. Auden' with the appropriate work:
options: Now the Leaves Are Falling Fast
Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe
questions.explanation: W.H. Auden wrote 'Now the Leaves Are Falling Fast'.

questions.question: Match the poet 'Kamala Das' with the appropriate work:
options: Now the Leaves Are Falling Fast
Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe
questions.explanation: Kamala Das wrote 'My Grandmother's House'.

questions.question: Match the poet 'John Donne' with the appropriate work:
options: Now the Leaves Are Falling Fast
Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe
questions.explanation: John Donne wrote 'Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe'.

questions.question:
Translate any five of the following sentences into English:
(i) वह अंग्रेजी बोलना नहीं जानता है।
(ii) हम लोग खा रहे हैं।
(iii) बच्चे हल्ला नहीं कर रहे हैं।
(iv) क्या रेणु गा रही है?
(v) उसने मुझे दौड़ना सिखाया।
(vi) राधा नाच रही है।
(vii) वह पिछले सोमवार से बीमार है।
(viii) तैरना एक कला है।
questions.explanation: (i) He does not know how to speak English. (ii) We are eating. (iii) Children are not making a noise. (iv) Is Renu singing? (v) He/She taught me how to run. (vi) Radha is dancing. (vii) He/She has been ill since last Monday. (viii) Swimming is an art.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
Kalidas is known as the Shakespeare of India. His name has been immortalized in the history of Sanskrit literature. He was at the head of the celebrated nine gems who adorned the court of Vikramaditya. The poems and dramas of Kalidas have elicited unreserved praise not only from Indian scholars but even from European critics like Max Muller. The age in which Kalidas flourished and the place where he was born are a matter of dispute. But true genius is independent of time and place and although the century of Kalidas is far more remote, his fame is shining with undiminished grandeur even in our days.
Questions: (i) Who is known as the Shakespeare of India? (ii) Who was Max Muller? (iii) Who adorned the court of Vikramaditya? (iv) Make sentence with the words 'independent' and 'century'.
OR Write a precis of the passage on friendship and give a suitable title.
questions.explanation: Comprehension answers: (i) Kalidas. (ii) A famous European critic/scholar. (iii) Kalidas and the other celebrated nine gems (Navaratnas). Precis title: The Value of True Friendship.
